notation.ko: Original opposite index with e0 ko=inl(m,!side).
notation.rho: n04bRootCutRadius(C.travel m)>0; common canonical half length.

central_domain_boundary.result: Transfer only actual forward chart, height± and absolute Jacobian± across the fixed reference cut. Subsequent inverse and canonical source estimates use the target index k on its genuine canonical strip.
central_domain_boundary.why: In the crossing case u>1. The opposite normalized canonical point (u,theta) is outside unitStrip, and its unnormalized point is beyond the opposite certified canonical half.
prohibited_shortcuts: Do not evaluate an opposite inverseRadial, inverseAngleDefect, sourceFactor or sourceFactorInverse unit-atom estimate at u>1.
The 256-line full-component germs concern chart, height and absolute forward Jacobian. They do not supply an arbitrary outside-strip stored inverse identity.
Do not identify the moving target half with a fixed reference half.

Absolute CurrentJets closeness does not by itself give uniform positive lower bounds for height or Jacobian. Nonvanishing comes from actual geometry/full-component regularity; reciprocal atoms are used quantitatively.
central_domain_boundary.safe_inverse_identity: Gz(Fz x)=x, G0(F0 r)=r and F0(G0 q)=q are used only on their actual mapped open sets.

membership_sequence.fact: x in moving target half implies x is in the original full negative component.
q=Fz x is in canonicalOpen k, and r=G0 q is in the reference physical target half.
Away from the fixed reference cut, x lies in exactly one of the two fixed reference halves of the same original component.
On the target reference half the current physical unit atoms directly supply jets. On the opposite reference half use Uo in unitStrip and physicalUnitPoint K ko Uo=x.
The exact stored metadata give canonical left=0 and right=rho, so the chartRadial atom is the root radial coordinate divided by rho, not by a physical width.

cross_half_point_and_germ_calculus.range_proof: Own current-half maps-to gives 0<v<1. The frozen normalized identity gives v^(3/2)+u^(3/2)=2, hence u>1. Reference maps-to gives 0<u_ref<1 at the opposite fixed-half point. One common CurrentJets shrink with |u-u_ref|<1/4 gives 1<u<5/4.
cross_half_point_and_germ_calculus.scalar_smoothness: All three scalar functions and eta/zeta reciprocals are ordinarily smooth on a fixed open neighborhood of [1,5/4]. Their every fixed finite derivative bound is universal, independent of component, state, rho and samples.
useful_derived_identities: hz(x)^2*Jz(x)=(K.height z ko x)^2*abs(planeJacobian(K.chart z ko)x)
cross_half_point_and_germ_calculus.derivative_cost_strategy: Compose with the opposite chartRadial atom directly in its physical unit variable. This avoids introducing rho^(-1) in u derivatives. Reconstruct the target unnormalized forward radial coordinate by multiplying by rho once. Physical derivatives of order a then cost the true opposite physical width to power -a; angular defects are used instead of the unbounded unwrapped angle.
cross_half_point_and_germ_calculus.status: Point/germ identities are frozen source results. The compact scalar range/jet estimate and its actual atom specialization are the next consumer and are not claimed formally proved here.

same_component_sample_comparison.exact_cell: K.cell k=n04CellAt D((K.physicalLeft k+K.physicalRight k)/2). The two half midpoints generally differ. Cell equality or sample equality is neither required nor asserted.
same_component_sample_comparison.preferred: For any nonnegative sample exponent, apply n04bActualTypedAtlas_negative_material_sample_comparison independently to k and ko at the same actual physical radius x.1. Both use full closed-component membership. This bounds Ek^P and Eo^Q by powers of T.E0(x.1); multiply/pack only after these two true inequalities.
same_component_sample_comparison.normalizer: For the literal H(x.1)/H(sample(K.cell k)) normalizer use the target k comparison. Its derivatives keep this same constant denominator and use the actual material power-jet formula. Do not switch to the opposite denominator.
same_component_sample_comparison.optional_sample_to_sample: The single constant A from negative_sample_endpointX compares each sample with any point of the closed component. At the shared component midpoint, the triangle inequality gives |X(sample k)-X(sample ko)|<=2*A. Use material_global_H_M_E0_rpow_bounded_X_shift at the two sample radii (each is in radialCore) if an explicit sample-to-sample weight comparison is needed.
same_component_sample_comparison.sample_core_warning: A sample is known to lie in its chosen cell and the radial core. It is not automatically a point of the original negative component, so never feed the sample itself into a full-component-only lemma without extra membership proof.
same_component_sample_comparison.preserved_indices: Raw optical host, correction cutoff host and K.cell k/K.cell ko stay distinct.
same_component_sample_comparison.floor: No E0>=1 is inferred from IsMaterialData alone. Any envelope packing that uses a floor must consume the actual earlier normalized material record/floor certificate.

local_material_pullback_interface.precise_existing_gap: n07a_materialPullback_zero_mixedDerivative and its bound currently take ContDiffOn infinity f on the whole annularOpen. A primitive field here is only supplied smooth on its actual moving open piece. That premise cannot be inserted without proof.
local_material_pullback_interface.minimal_new_reusable_statement_in_math: For each N, fixed hT supplies C_N>=0, independent of an open U, f and y, such that f smooth on U, Phi(y)=(T.radius(y.1),y.2) in U and all physical mixed jets a+b<=N at Phi(y) bounded by M>=0 imply ||D^k(f compose Phi)(y)||<=C_N*M for every k<=N.
proof_using_existing_coefficients: Let U be the true current physical piece and work on its open preimage under Phi.

Use contDiffOn_mixedDerivative on U, then at the single true point compose the radial slice locally. A local open neighborhood may justify the derivative identity; its radius does not enter any numerical constant.
The existing one-dimensional ordered-partition formula gives the same sum over c of mixedDerivative(c.length,b,f)(Phi y) times n07aRadiusJetCoefficient(T,c)(y.1).
n07aRadiusJetCoefficient_bounded is genuinely global and independent of U/f/y. Use its finite prefix once, without replacing the actual T.radius.
Apply norm_iteratedFDeriv_le_of_mixedDerivative on Phi-preimage U. Its factor 2^k is absorbed into C_N.
local_material_pullback_interface.finite_orders: This radius pullback does not increase the physical derivative order. The N+2 reserve belongs to primitive-direction/Jacobian differentiation before this step.
local_material_pullback_interface.quantifiers: Choose C_N and all finite-prefix scalar constants before piece, state and point. Higher state orders r_N and polynomial degree d_N may depend on N, as allowed by materialJets. The low neighborhood is the one fixed earlier by normalized radial closeness, not reselected at each N.

fixed_reference_cut_case.statement: If x lies on the fixed reference cut while remaining inside the target moving half, it is not in either open reference half.
fixed_reference_cut_case.route: The actual moving domain is open. Approach x from the opposite fixed half while staying in that domain. Actual full-component chart/height regularity and nonzero Jacobian make their finite ordinary jets continuous at x; material envelopes and the finite state factor are continuous there. Uniform pointwise inequalities extend by continuity.
fixed_reference_cut_case.constants: No chosen local neighborhood radius enters a bound, and no equality of reference/current cuts is assumed.
fixed_reference_cut_case.exclusions: True roots and the current artificial cut are not in that target open materialJets domain. They are handled separately only for the global C3 transport conclusion.
